identity.title: GOODS-ALMA: Optically dark ALMA galaxies shed light on a cluster in formation at z = 3.5

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the spectroscopic scan follow-up of five of the six sources with ALMA band 4. All are detected in the 2 mm continuum with signal-to-noise ratios higher than eight.

redshift_or_distance.value: AGS11 and AGS15 assumed z = 3.472; AGS25 z_phot = 4.64

distance_source.value: assumed from the redshift peak (AGS11, AGS15); ZFOURGE photometric redshift (AGS25)

question.value: What are the properties of the six optically dark galaxies in the GOODS-ALMA survey, what are their redshifts, and do they trace a proto-cluster at z~3.5?

evidence.quote: Studying the connection of optically dark ALMA galaxies with the formation of large-scale structures is the main goal of the present paper.

using the spectroscopic scan mode in Cycle 7 (project 2018.1.01079.S PI: M. Franco)
We followed up these five optically dark sources with ALMA band 4 using the spectroscopic scan mode in Cycle 7
The band 4 observations were performed by combining four tunings to cover a total frequency range of 137.2–165.8 GHz
The CO(6-5) line with a rest-frame frequency of $\nu_{\rm RF}$ = 806.7 GHz gives a $z_{spec}^{AGS4}$ = 3.566

analysis_steps.goal: Reduce band 4 scan data and search for lines

analysis_steps.goal: Determine spectroscopic redshifts of AGS4 and AGS17

method.value: Identify the single line as CO(6-5) using SED/PDF of photometric redshift, far-IR SED dust temperature, L_IR-L_CO relation, [CI] non-detection, and redshift-peak probability

evidence.quote: we decided to favor the CO(6-5) transition from a purely probabilistic point of view.

assumptions.value: Typical dust temperature ~38-40 K at these redshifts (Schreiber18)

evidence.quote: close to the typical dust temperature $T_{\rm dust}$ $\sim$ 40 K at $z$ = 3.5 (cite: Schreiber18)

validation.value: consistency with photometric redshift PDF and 4000 A break

evidence.quote: gives a $z_{spec}^{AGS4}$ = 3.566, which agrees with the 4000 Å discontinuity in the optical SED.

analysis_steps.goal: Deblend optical/NIR photometry and derive photometric redshifts and stellar masses

method.value: De-blend neighbors, fit SEDs with EAzY (redshift) and FAST++ (mass; delayed exponentially declining SFH, Calzetti attenuation)

evidence.quote: derived from the observed optical to mid-infrared SED fitted with `FAST++` assuming a delayed exponentially declining SFH and a (cite: Calzetti00) attenuation law
We use cosmological parameters of H$_{0}$ = 70 km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, $\Omega_{M}$ = 0.3, and $\Omega_{\Lambda}$ = 0.7.

validation.value: AGS24 mass tested with varied SFH and attenuation laws (FAST++, CIGALE); stays within 10^11.31-10^11.52

evidence.quote: the stellar mass of AGS24 remains within 10$^{11.31}$ and 10$^{11.52}$ M$_{\odot}$

claims.hypothesis: Optically dark ALMA galaxies trace an overdensity
claims.experiment: Redshifts, density map and Monte Carlo test
claims.result: 4 of 6 optically dark galaxies in a 5 arcmin2 region at z~3.5; chance 0.4%
claims.finding: They trace a proto-cluster at z~3.5

evidence.quote: four of the six optically dark galaxies reside in a small region of 5 arcmin$^2$ only.

claims.result: most massive non-AGN galaxy at z>3 in field, at density peak
claims.finding: candidate BCG in a virializing proto-cluster

evidence.quote: It falls in the very center of the peak of the galaxy surface density

claims.experiment: Compare SED PDFs, dust temperature, L_IR-L_CO, redshift peak
claims.finding: CO(6-5) favoured, though AGS17 CO(5-4) not strictly excluded

evidence.quote: despite the fact that we cannot strictly rule out the possibility that we are here observing the CO(5-4) transition

why_this_data.value: Spectroscopic scan to give broad redshift coverage with at least one CO line

evidence.quote: that ensures a broad redshift coverage from $z$ = 2 to $z$ = 5

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CO(7-6) and H2O rejected for AGS4; CO(5-4) disfavoured for AGS17

limitations_admitted.value: Single lines cannot give definitive redshifts

evidence.quote: One ALMA spectral line alone is not sufficient to obtain a definitive spectroscopic redshift for AGS4.
